body.heading: Why walking works
paragraphs: Walking changes several things at once: your location, your breathing, the rhythm of your body, and the input to your eyes. After twenty minutes staring at a problem at close range, distance — literal and mental — is often what was missing.
It does not need to be a “proper” walk. Around the block, to the shop and back, or a loop of the school field all count. The point is movement plus a change of scene, not exercise targets.

body.heading: Make it your default pause
paragraphs: When you notice yourself re-reading the same line, snapping at small things, or refreshing feeds without seeing them, treat it as a signal: walk first, then decide. Many problems are smaller after ten minutes of daylight.
Leave the headphones off sometimes, if it is safe to do so. The unaccompanied version lets your mind wander, and wandering minds are famously where solutions turn up.

takeaway: Stuck or wound up? Ten minutes of walking before you decide anything.
